name: How to decide between roof repair and replacement for storm damage in Alvarado

step.name: Step 1: Document the Damage Thoroughly — Before doing anything else, take clear photos and videos of all visible damage, inside and out. This includes missing shingles, dents, leaks, or any debris. This documentation is crucial for insurance claims and helps us get a full picture of what happened. It helps determine if the issue is localized or indicates broader problems across the roof system, such as compromised fasteners or flashings.

step.name: Step 2: Get a Professional Roof Inspection — Have an experienced roofing professional, like our team at Discounted Roofing Co., perform a comprehensive inspection. We'll look beyond the obvious, checking accessible roof surfaces, gutters, flashings, penetrations, and even your attic for signs of hidden damage or structural compromise. This helps clarify if the damage is isolated, recurring, or widespread, which is vital for evaluating remaining service life.

step.name: Step 3: Understand the Underlying Issues — A good assessment will determine if the problem is just cosmetic or if it points to a deeper issue that affects your roof's ability to protect your home. We'll assess the condition of your underlying deck and whether a repair can truly restore watertight performance for a reasonable duration. Don't treat a visible stain as the entire problem; always look for the root cause.

step.name: Step 4: Compare Repair, Partial, and Full Replacement Scopes — Based on the inspection, you'll get clear options. We'll help you compare the scope of repair, partial replacement (if applicable), and full replacement. We'll discuss expected service life implications for each option, ensuring you understand the pros and cons of extending the life of your current roof versus investing in a new one that can last decades, especially for harsh Texas weather.

step.name: Step 5: Verify Contractor Credentials and Contract Details — Before committing, always verify your chosen contractor's licensing and insurance. Get multiple written estimates with detailed scopes of work, including material specifications, removal, disposal, and any deck repairs. Make sure the contract describes the work, materials, completion timing, and price clearly. This helps avoid frequent mistakes like comparing apples to oranges on estimates or selecting solely on the lowest price.
